title: Eye and ear
goal: Use everyday idioms built on göz, el, kulak, ağız, baş, yüz and burun, each with the case it takes.

intro.text: Many Turkish idioms rest on a part of the body: *göz kulak olmak* (to keep an eye on: to be eye and ear), *ağzından kaçırmak* (to let slip: to let it escape from your mouth). Learn each with its case: *çocuklara göz kulak ol*, *sözlerime kulak asmadı*.

vocab.en: to keep an eye on, to look after (dative: çocuklara göz kulak olmak)
to like, to take to (hiçbirini gözüm tutmadı: I didn't like any of them)
to be overlooked, to slip past (gözümden kaçmış: I missed it)
to join forces, to work together
to take no notice of, to ignore (dative)
to let slip, to blurt out
to happen to (someone), usually something bad
to indulge, to give too much leeway (dative)
to be badly missed (köyüm burnumda tütüyor: I really miss my village)

exercises.question: Your neighbour asks: *Hafta sonu kedime göz kulak olur musun?* What does she want?
options: To have you look after her cat at the weekend
To have you find her cat at the weekend
To have you take her cat to the vet
To have you keep her cat out of sight

why.1: Finding would be *bulmak*. *Göz kulak olmak* is to watch over something.
why.2: Nothing is said about a vet: she wants someone to watch over the cat.
why.3: *Göz kulak olmak* is about watching, not hiding: be eye and ear to it.

exercises.explain: *Göz kulak olmak* takes the dative: *kedime göz kulak olmak*, to look after my cat. *Olur musun?* is the usual friendly request.

exercises.en: Sorry, I couldn't help overhearing your conversation.

accept: misafiri

reject.why: *Kulak misafiri* is a compound, so *misafir* takes `-(s)I`, as in *Türk kahvesi*.

exercises.hint: An ear that is a guest…
exercises.explain: *Kulak misafiri olmak* (to be an ear guest) is to overhear. What you overhear takes the dative: *konuşmanıza*.

exercises.prompt: Will you keep an eye on the children while I'm out?
accept: Ben yokken çocuklara göz kulak olur musun?
Ben yokken çocuklara göz kulak olur musunuz?
[yokken|dışarıdayken|evde yokken] çocuklara göz kulak [olur musun|olur musunuz|olabilir misin|olabilir misiniz]?
Ben yokken çocuklara göz kulak olabilir misin?
Ben yokken çocuklara göz kulak olabilir misiniz?
Ben dışarıdayken çocuklara göz kulak [olur musun|olur musunuz|olabilir misin|olabilir misiniz]?
Ben evde yokken çocuklara göz kulak [olur musun|olur musunuz|olabilir misin|olabilir misiniz]?
Çocuklara (ben) [yokken|dışarıdayken|evde yokken] göz kulak [olur musun|olur musunuz|olabilir misin|olabilir misiniz]?
(Ben) [yokken|dışarıdayken|evde yokken] çocuklara sen göz kulak [olur musun|olabilir misin]?
(Ben) [yokken|dışarıdayken|evde yokken] çocuklara siz göz kulak [olur musunuz|olabilir misiniz]?
Sen (ben) [yokken|dışarıdayken|evde yokken] çocuklara göz kulak [olur musun|olabilir misin]?
Siz (ben) [yokken|dışarıdayken|evde yokken] çocuklara göz kulak [olur musunuz|olabilir misiniz]?

reject.answer: Ben yokken çocukları göz kulak olur musun?

exercises.explain: The idiom takes the dative: *çocuklara göz kulak olmak*. A request in the aorist, *olur musun?*, is the usual polite form.

accept: How did we miss this mistake?
How did we miss this error?
How did we overlook this [mistake|error]?
How could we [miss|overlook] this [mistake|error]?
How come we [missed|overlooked] this [mistake|error]?
How did we not [see|notice|spot] this [mistake|error]?
How did this [mistake|error] [escape our notice|escape us|get past us|slip past us|go unnoticed]?
exercises.explain: *Gözden kaçmak*: the mistake is the subject, and it escapes from our eye, *gözümüzden*. English turns it round: we missed it.

exercises.en: I let the surprise slip, I'm so sorry.
exercises.explain: *Ağzından kaçırmak* is to let slip. *Gözden kaçmak* (with *kaçmak*) is to overlook, and *elinden kaçırmak* is to miss a chance: *fırsatı elimden kaçırdım*.

exercises.question: Which sentence means **She's very good at keeping secrets**?

why.2: *Gözü açık* (open-eyed) means sharp, hard to fool.
why.3: *Burnu havada* (nose in the air) means stuck-up.

exercises.explain: *Ağzı sıkı* (tight-mouthed) is someone who keeps secrets. The opposite is *ağzı gevşek*, a blabbermouth.

exercises.prompt: Use the idiom with *burun*: I really miss my mother's cooking.
accept: Annemin yemekleri burnumda tütüyor.
annemin yemeği burnumda tütüyor.
annemin yaptığı yemekler burnumda tütüyor.
Benim annemin [yemekleri|yemeği|yaptığı yemekler] burnumda tütüyor.

reject.why: That's correct Turkish, but the task asks for the idiom: *Annemin yemekleri burnumda tütüyor*.
That's correct Turkish, but the task asks for the idiom: *Annemin yemekleri burnumda tütüyor*.
*Burnunda* is his or her nose. You are the one who misses them: *burnumda*.

exercises.explain: The thing you miss is the subject; the possessive on *burun* says who misses it: *burnumda*, with the vowel loss of [A1 unit 9](gp-vowel-loss).

exercises.prompt: Çocuğa bu kadar yüz verme, sonra sözünü dinlemez.
accept: Do not spoil the child so much, or later he will not listen to you.
Do not [spoil|indulge] the [child|kid] [so much|like that|this much], [or|otherwise] [he|she] will not listen to you later.
Do not spoil the child so much, or later she will not listen to you.
Do not spoil the child so much, otherwise later [he|she] will not listen to you.
Do not spoil the child like that, [or|otherwise] later [he|she] will not listen to you.
Do not spoil the child this much, [or|otherwise] later [he|she] will not listen to you.
Do not spoil the kid [so much|like that|this much], [or|otherwise] later [he|she] will not listen to you.
Do not indulge the [child|kid] [so much|like that|this much], [or|otherwise] later [he|she] will not listen to you.
Do not [spoil|indulge] the [child|kid] [so much|like that|this much]; [he|she] will not listen to you later.
Do not give the [child|kid] so much leeway, [or|otherwise] [he|she] will not listen to you later.
Do not [spoil|indulge] the [child|kid] [so much|like that|this much], [or|otherwise] [he|she] will not do as you say later.
If you [spoil|indulge] the [child|kid] [so much|like that|this much], [he|she] will not listen to you later.
exercises.explain: *Yüz vermek* (to give face) is to indulge someone until they take liberties. *Sözünü dinlemek* (to listen to your word) is to do as you're told.

exercises.text: Bu işi kendi başıma yapamam; hep birlikte el ele ___.
exercises.en: I can't do this job on my own; we all need to join forces.

accept: vermeliyiz

reject.why: *Vermeliyim* is **I** must. Joining forces takes several people: *vermeliyiz*.

exercises.explain: *El ele vermek* (to give hand to hand) is to join forces; **we need to** is `-mAlI` with the first person plural: *vermeliyiz*.

exercises.title: Düğün hazırlıkları
exercises.passage:
Sevgili Ece,

Kuzenim Selin'in düğününe iki hafta kaldı ve bütün aile el ele verdi. Annem her şeye göz kulak oluyor; babam da elinden geleni yapıyor, ama listeleri hep karıştırıyor.

Dün başıma gelmeyen kalmadı. Selin'e sürpriz bir parti hazırlıyorduk; küçük kardeşim Can, akşam yemeğinde her şeyi ağzından kaçırdı! Selin de mutfaktan konuşmamıza kulak misafiri olmuş. Annem, “Bu çocuğa çok yüz verdik.” dedi. Haklı: Can'ın hiç ağzı sıkı değil.

Neyse, sen ne zaman geliyorsun? İzmir burnumda tütüyor; düğünden sonra birkaç gün size gelmek istiyorum.

Sevgiler,

Elif

glossary.en: everything that could go wrong did
love (at the end of a letter)

exercises.translation: Dear Ece, There are two weeks to go before my cousin Selin's wedding, and the whole family has joined forces. My mother is keeping an eye on everything, and my father is doing his best, but he keeps mixing up the lists. Yesterday everything that could go wrong did. We were preparing a surprise party for Selin, and my little brother Can let it all slip at dinner! And Selin had overheard our conversation from the kitchen. My mother said, “We've spoiled this child.” She's right: Can can't keep a secret at all. Anyway, when are you coming? I really miss Izmir; I'd like to come and stay with you for a few days after the wedding. Love, Elif

questions.q: What is the whole family doing?
questions.explain: *Bütün aile el ele verdi*: they have joined forces.
*Her şeyi ağzından kaçırdı*: he let it all slip. It was Selin who overheard.

questions.q: What does Elif's mother mean by *Bu çocuğa çok yüz verdik*?
options: We've been too hard on this child
We've given this child too many presents
questions.explain: *Yüz vermek*: to indulge someone until they take liberties.

questions.q: Why does Elif want to go to Izmir?
questions.explain: *İzmir burnumda tütüyor*: she misses Izmir badly.

exercises.task: Someone in your family is getting married next month. Write three or four sentences about the preparations. Use at least three idioms from this lesson (*el ele vermek*, *göz kulak olmak*, *ağzından kaçırmak*, *başına gelmek*…).
models: Kuzenimin düğünü için bütün aile el ele verdi. Annem her şeye göz kulak oluyor, ben de elimden geleni yapıyorum. Ama dün kardeşim sürpriz partiyi ağzından kaçırdı; artık sürpriz kalmadı!
Ablam gelecek ay evleniyor. Babam hiçbir şeyin gözden kaçmasını istemiyor; listeleri üç kez kontrol ediyor. Bu hafta başıma gelmeyen kalmadı, ama yine de çok mutluyuz.
checklist: Each idiom keeps its own case: *her şeye göz kulak olmak*, *bir sözüne kulak asmamak*
The possessive on the body part matches the person: *elimden geleni*, *ağzından kaçırdı*
